what_it_does: Modern high-performance processors (called out-of-order superscalar cores) execute instructions in a flexible, reordered way to keep the hardware busy — making it very hard to track exactly which instruction is doing what, and when, for security analysis. Existing research tools use simplified simulations that miss the real timing pressures and resource conflicts that happen on actual chips. FireGuard is a new hardware design that adds programmable monitoring pathways directly inside a real processor, so engineers can observe fine-grained, instruction-level behavior without slowing the chip down or creating new bottlenecks. It also includes extensions to the chip's instruction language (so software can communicate with the monitor) and has been evaluated against three real commercial processors — Apple M1-Pro, Huawei Kirin-960, and Intel i7-12700F — to show it is practical to build.
